description: A four-in, four-out switch whose wiring is changed by trigger inputs or by one of 128 stored patterns, with a map showing which input reaches which output

params.text: Chooses which stored pattern the step jack advances through, 1 to 128; at 0 the patterns are switched off and the display shows dashes

inputs.text: A trigger here puts the chosen pattern back to its first step and puts the input-to-output map back to straight through
A trigger here moves the chosen pattern on one step, which applies whichever map control that step holds
A trigger here exchanges the two inputs feeding outputs 1 and 2
A trigger here exchanges the two inputs feeding outputs 1 and 3
A trigger here gives every output a new input at random
One of the four signals to be routed; whichever output it is mapped to carries it unchanged
A trigger here exchanges the two inputs feeding outputs 3 and 4
A trigger here exchanges the two inputs feeding outputs 2 and 4
A trigger here undoes the last map change, back through as many as 128 of them
A trigger here exchanges the two inputs feeding outputs 2 and 3
A trigger here moves every input up one output, wrapping round at the top
A trigger here redoes the last change that was undone, through as many as 128 undos
A trigger here exchanges the two inputs feeding outputs 1 and 4
A trigger here moves every input down one output, wrapping round at the bottom
A trigger here puts the map back to straight through, input 1 to output 1 and so on

outputs.text: Carries whichever input is mapped to it at the moment, unchanged

notes: the black screen draws a line from each input to the output it currently reaches, so the wiring can be read off the panel
the map controls and the stored patterns can be used together; a pattern step applies the same kinds of change the jacks do
every trigger jack fires on any move away from exactly 0V, so a negative-going signal fires it as well
an output whose mapped input has no cable in it holds the last voltage it carried
menu: Match cable colors — draws each line on the map in the colour of the cable patched to that input; the setting is not saved with the patch
Use DD cable color scheme - Light — replaces Rack's cable colour list with five colours of the maker's, after a confirmation step; the item ends in Dark under the Rack dark-panel setting
